newsitem.title: USA: Givaudan Roure to end U.S. chemical operations.
newsitem.headline: Givaudan Roure to end U.S. chemical operations.

text.p: Givaudan-Roure, a fragrances and flavors manufacturing unit of Roche Holding Ltd, said Wednesday it was discontinuing its chemical manufacturing operations at its Clifton, N.J. facility.
The phaseout of operations is expected to be carried out over a 12 to 18 month period, effective immediately and will affect 200 employees at the facility, it said.
Givaudan-Roure said it took the step as part of the company's long-term business strategy "to redirect U.S. chemical manufacturing capabilities within its global network."

The Clifton plant makes "aroma" chemicals that are used in making perfume and household products, a company spokesman said. The company said customers curently purchasing Givaudan-Roure chemicals made at the Clifton site may continue to be supplied by its global network.
The company has chemical plants in Vernier, Switzerland; Sant Celoni, Spain; and Lyon, France.
